rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.e1: This is a study by Nikolai Grigoriev, from 1930. White to play and win.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.e2: White starts by advancing the b-pawn just one square. The c-pawn still keeps its move in reserve.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.e3: The black king goes to a5, next to its pawn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.e4: Now the white pawns no longer have a quiet move to pass the turn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.a8a7.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.a8a7.2: The black pawn advances to b4. Notice: the white king on a7 takes a6 and b6 from the black king.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.a8a7.3: The c-pawn advances. The black king on a5 has nowhere to go and is not in check: stalemate, a draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.a8b7.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.a8b7.2: The black pawn advances to b4. From b7, the white king controls a6 and b6, the black king's escape squares.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.a8b7.3: With the c-pawn advance, the black king is trapped on a5, not in check. It is stalemate, and the game is drawn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.b3b4.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.b3b4.2: The black king retreats to a6. If the c-pawn advances, the black pawn captures it: the reserve tempo is gone.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.c3c4.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.err.c3c4.2: The black pawn captures on c4. One white pawn is left against the black king, which is close to it: a draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.p: White to play. Think and suggest a move, or tap {verResposta}
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.certo: Exactly! The king passes the turn without taking any square from the black king.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to bring the king to b8: it passes the turn without taking squares from the black king.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.fora: That move is not one we are studying here. Let's go back to the position.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.volta: Let's go back to the position. Suggest another move or tap {verResposta}
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l1: A move like this is called a waiting move: it changes nothing important and just hands back the turn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l2: Now Black must play, and every Black move makes things worse: zugzwang.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l3: The black pawn advances to b4.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l4: Now the c-pawn does advance. It becomes free, and the black king cannot go to b5.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l5: The black king goes back to b6, near the c4 pawn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l6: The white king sets off to the right, and the black king follows, always facing it.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l7: In the corner, the white king goes down the h-file. The black king cannot follow there: the c4 pawn would advance and promote.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l8: Along the third rank, the white king comes back and reaches d3, next to the c4 pawn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l9: The b4 pawn will fall, and White wins.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l10: Let's go back to the question position. Why b8, and not a7 or b7?
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l11: On a7 or b7, the white king would take a6 and b6 from the black king. After the pawns advance, it would be stalemate.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.l12: Remember: when the pawns can no longer pass the turn, the king makes the waiting move.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex1.curiosidades: Nikolai Grigoriev (1895–1938), from Moscow, was a player and composer of endgame studies, above all pawn endings. This study is from 1930: the win depends on a king waiting move.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.e1: Now let's look at another example. Here no pawn can move: they are all blocked.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.e2: White wants to capture the pawns on c5 and c6. The black king on b7 protects c6.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.e3: With no reserve tempo, the king takes care of the turn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.f6e7.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.f6e7.2: The black king goes to a7: three squares between the kings on the seventh rank, and Black has just moved.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.f6g7.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.f6g7.2: The black king goes to a7: five squares between the kings on the seventh rank, an odd number, and Black has just moved.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.f6e6.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.f6e6.2: The black king goes to a6, on the same rank. If the white king goes to d7 or f7, the black king returns to b7.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.f6g6.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.f6g6.2: The black king waits on a6. If the white king steps to f7, it answers on b7; if it goes to g7, on a7.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.f6e5.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.f6e5.2: The black king goes to a7. If the white king returns to d6, the black king goes to b6 and protects c5 and c6.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.f6f5.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.f6f5.2: The black king goes to a7 and waits. If the white king returns to f6, the black king takes b6, next to both pawns.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.f6g5.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.err.f6g5.2: The black king waits on a7 and copies every step: if the white king goes to g6, it goes to a6; if to f6, to b6.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.p: White to play. Think and suggest a move, or tap {verResposta}
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.certo: Exactly! The king steps back to f7, on the black king's rank, with three squares between them.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to step the king back to f7, on the black king's rank: three squares between them, and Black to move.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.fora: That move is not one we are studying here. Let's go back to the position.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.volta: Let's go back to the position. Suggest another move or tap {verResposta}
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l1: Notice: the white king stepped back. It seems to waste time, but it is a waiting move.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l2: Three empty squares between the kings on the seventh rank, an odd number: White has the distant opposition.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l3: The black king goes to a7.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l4: The white king follows to e7: again, three squares between the kings.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l5: The black king returns to b7, next to the c6 pawn.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l6: Now the white king steps into d7: direct opposition, and the black king must give way.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l7: The black king goes to b6 and protects both pawns, c5 and c6.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l8: The white king goes to d6 and attacks c5 and c6. Any black king move leaves one of them unprotected.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l9: The black king goes to a5, and the white king captures the c5 pawn. White wins.
rot.waiting.ideia.ex2.l10: Let's go back to the starting position. Stepping back to f7 passed the turn to the black king, like a reserve tempo, but with the king.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.1: First position: the same structure, but now the black king is on b6 and the white one on f7.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.2: There is more than one way to win. Let's look at the waiting move on the edge.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.3: The white king goes to e8, on the edge: a waiting move.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.4: The black king goes to a7.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.5: The white king answers on e7: three empty squares between the kings on the seventh rank, and Black to move.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.6: The black king returns to b7, and the white king steps into d7: direct opposition.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.7: You already know the rest: on d6, the white king attacks c5 and c6, and one of them will fall.
rot.waiting.demos.borda.8: The c5 pawn falls. On the edge or away from it, the king waiting move handed over the turn at the right time.
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.1: Now thinking from Black's side, and the board has turned. In Grigoriev's study, the white king went to a7.
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.2: It came closer, but took two squares from the black king: a6 and b6.
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.3: The black pawn advances to b4.
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.4: If the c-pawn advances, the black king has no moves and is not in check.
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.5: It is stalemate, and stalemate is a draw.
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.6: And what if White captures on b4?
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.7: The black king captures back and, on the next move, also captures the b3 pawn. It is a draw.
rot.waiting.demos.afogamento.8: In defence, an attacking king that comes too close may stalemate the defending king. That is why, in the study, the white king waited on b8.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.h8g8.1: The king waits too early, while the g-pawn is still on g2.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.h8g8.2: The black pawn advances to g4 and trades the pawns: Black holds the draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.f3f4.1: The f-pawn advances and offers itself for capture.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.f3f4.2: The black pawn captures on f4. One white pawn is left, and the black king catches it: a draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.g2g4.1: The g-pawn advances two squares and spends the reserve tempo.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.err.g2g4.2: The black king goes to h6. The g-pawns are blocked, and Black holds the draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.h8g7.1: The king comes closer, but takes g6 and h6 from the black king.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.h8g7.2: The black pawn advances to g4. If the f-pawn advances, the black king has no moves: stalemate.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.h8h7.1: On h7, the white king is too close and controls g6 and h6.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.h8h7.2: After the black pawn advances to g4, the f-pawn can no longer advance without stalemating the black king.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.f3f4.1: The f-pawn advances too soon, within reach of the black pawn.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.f3f4.2: The black pawn captures on f4 and, after the exchange, the black king catches the remaining pawn.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.g3g4.1: The g-pawn advances with check and spends the last reserve tempo.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v2.err.g3g4.2: The black king retreats to h6 and stays next to the pawns: Black holds the draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v3.err.f3g4.1: The f-pawn captures on g4, with check, and trades the pawns.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v3.err.f3g4.2: The black king captures back. One white pawn is left, with the black king near it: a draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v3.err.g8g7.1: The king leaves g8, but the black pawn can still capture on f3.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v3.err.g8g7.2: With the capture on f3, the black pawn is free and close to promoting: Black wins.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v3.err.g8f7.1: The king goes to f7, and the f3 pawn is still attacked by the black pawn.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.v3.err.g8f7.2: The black pawn captures on f3 and runs to promote. The white king is too far away.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.enunciado: Play as White and find the best move.
rot.waiting.pratica.ataque.fim: The pawn kept its tempo, the king waited without stalemating, and the f-pawn became free.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.f3e2.1: The king goes to e2, close to the white king, but at the wrong distance.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.f3e2.2: The white king goes to a2: three squares between the kings on the second rank, and White has the opposition.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.f3g2.1: The king goes to g2, on the second rank, but too far from the white king.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.f3g2.2: The white king goes to c2: three empty squares between the kings, and White keeps the opposition.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.f3e3.1: The king advances to e3 and leaves the white king's rank.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.f3e3.2: The white king has only one defence: going up to a3, on the black king's rank. With it, White holds the draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.f3g3.1: The king goes to g3, far from the queenside pawns.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.f3g3.2: The white king has more than one way to wait, and the black king reaches the pawns too late: a draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.f3e4.1: The king advances to e4 and abandons the second rank.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.f3e4.2: The white king steps back to a2, a waiting move like the one your king missed. It is the only defence, and it is enough.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.f3f4.1: The king retreats to f4 and moves away from the white king.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.f3f4.2: The white king goes to a2 and passes the turn. Now it is the black king that must give way: a draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.f3g4.1: The king retreats to g4, far from the pawns it needs to attack.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.err.f3g4.2: The white king waits near its pawns, and the black king cannot get in: a draw.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.enunciado: Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.waiting.pratica.defesa.fim: Your king stepped back to f2, on the white king's rank, and kept the distant opposition.
